name: rp2350 production: secure boot (signed images, boot key hash in OTP)
summary: The bootrom boots only images signed with your key: the SHA-256 hash of its public key is written to OTP and secure boot is switched on in OTP. OTP rows are one-time programmable; nothing here can be undone.
build: CONFIG_RH_PRODUCTION=y in the project's configuration and RH_SECURE_BOOT_SIGNING_KEY naming the secp256k1 PEM key; the build signs the image and writes build/output/<program>.otp.json. Set RH_PICO_OTP_JSON to that file. Keep the key: once its hash is in OTP the board boots nothing else.

steps.description: load the OTP rows the signed build produced: BOOTKEY0 (the SHA-256 hash of the signing public key), BOOT_FLAGS1.KEY_VALID for key 0, and CRIT1.SECURE_BOOT_ENABLE. The board must be in BOOTSEL mode and reachable by picotool over USB

notes: The OTP file's contents are printed above in full: every row in it is burned. Read them before typing the board name.
The image is written after the OTP rows, while the board is still in BOOTSEL mode; it must be the signed image built with the same key, or the board will not boot it.

Not done by this plan, and each irreversible on its own: CRIT1.DEBUG_DISABLE (turns off SWD), and moving the device keystore from flash into OTP rows (planned; OTP rows cannot be rewritten, so a rotated key would use up a row per epoch). Until then the keystore lives in the last two flash sectors, readable over SWD unless debug is disabled.
picotool must be built with mbedtls (the SDK's lib/mbedtls submodule) for the build to sign, and with USB support for this step to reach the board.
